explorer.title: European Crime Data Explorer
explorer.subtitle: Analyze crime patterns and trends across all European countries. Use the filters to explore different crime types, years, and metrics.
explorer.trendsDesc: This chart shows how the selected crime type has changed over 16 years across the top 5 countries with the highest average rates. The lines help identify long-term trends — whether crime is increasing, decreasing, or remaining stable in different regions.
explorer.animatedDesc: Watch how {crime} rates have evolved across Europe from 2008 to 2023. Darker colors indicate higher crime rates per 100,000 inhabitants. This animation helps visualize geographical patterns and how they shift over time.
explorer.yearToYearDesc: This heatmap shows how crime rates changed from one year to the next across Europe. Green means crime decreased, red means crime increased. Values show percentage change compared to the previous year.
explorer.fingerprints: Criminal Fingerprints: Country vs European Average
explorer.fingerprintsDesc: This heatmap compares each country's crime rates to the European average (2019-2023 data). Green means below average, red means above average. Values show how many times higher or lower than the EU average (1.0 = exactly average). This visualization reveals each country's unique "criminal fingerprint" — their distinctive pattern of crime types.

overview.title: Overview
overview.content: This project explores crime trends across European countries using publicly available data from Eurostat and provides a reproducible exploratory analysis of crime patterns across Europe. The objective was to apply core data science skills — data cleaning, preprocessing, exploratory analysis, visualization, and interpretation — to produce meaningful insights about crime patterns.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.content: The project uses crime categories defined by the ICCS (International Classification of Crime Statistics) framework, allowing consistent comparison across countries and years. Crime rates are normalized per 100,000 inhabitants to enable fair comparison between countries of different population sizes. This project is purely descriptive and does not make causal claims.

scope.title: Scope & Limitations
scope.content: This project covers 25 crime categories across 39 European countries, mainly from 2008 to 2023, but also using historic data from 1993-2007. Note that reporting practices and legal definitions vary between countries, which may affect comparability. Some data points may be missing or show anomalies due to differences in national reporting systems.

credits.title: Credits
credits.content: This project was developed as part of the Data Science course at the University of Tartu. Crime data sourced from Eurostat crime and criminal justice datasets. Geographic boundaries provided by EuroGeographics.
